Ever since the stagnation caused by the Meteoric Starfall, the terminator line had become the lifeline of the Salsottians.

When it all started, people still took the shifting of day and night for granted. The line of dawn and dusk swept across the earth, climbed over mountains and ravines, brought dawn to those still awake, and sent sunset to those who would soon sleep... But when the rhythm of light and darkness slowed down, day and night were no longer familiar, and the seemingly eternal heat and coldness were like the quagmire of hell, slowly burying all lives entrapped within. This was why the Salsottian people, barely surviving at the time, boarded the floating mobile city and began their chase with dawn and dusk.

Climbing atop the observation deck of the mobile city of Tumbleweed and looking in the direction that they were moving, daylight lies ahead and dark night behind.

The pursuit of "Tumbleweed" is not only for survival but also for a dignified life. When it moved faster than the terminator line, then the early morning light would march into the afternoon; when slower than the terminator line, then the dusk light would fade into the late night. In this way, the naturally optimistic Salsottian managed to restore every day to its original state. The romance in their bloodline blessed them with the easygoing spirit to sing leisurely in peaceful afternoons and sleep soundly on starry nights.

However, this voyage of tenacity and perseverance would, at last, come to its final downfall, and the ruins of the once mobile city were eventually left far behind by the ever-shifting terminator line.

Years later, the two moving cities that had never met each other would finally stand against each other, with their respective turrets among the wreckage still aimed in opposition. One of the two cities must have crossed half of the planet to the other one and started the initial incursion. Traces of brutal warfare between the two cities were still occasionally discernible under the sand dunes, which merged with unnameable hatred and morphed together into the same ruins.

Planet Salsotto kept its silence. And ever since a certain unknown time, the duration of each of its rotation cycles had somehow gradually decreased, ushering in its own self-healing in an unpopulated future.

14958180579543693231: To save the living from the clutches of the demons from beyond, our ancestor Graphia harnessed the power of the Phantasmoon Games, using the sea as her canvas to hide the planet within the "World in Canvas." But all things come with a cost. This act of salvation also bound an eternal curse to the bloodline of the Graphia family. The daughter shall be stripped of her flesh, trapped unto death within her bed. The son shall be peeled of his soul, left to wander the wastelands. The "Weathering Curse" first manifested in Graphia's body, then passed to our ancestors, Huear and Lumirae, becoming known to the world. As the years go by, the female descendants' bodies suffer corrosion: limbs wither, skin cracks and splits, like a decaying painting, peeling away layer by layer, turning to dust. The male descendants' minds are tortured, trapped in a daze, unable to recognize themselves, ultimately lost to madness. However, our family bears the responsibility of protecting this planet. We cannot bring ourselves to sever our bloodline and abandon this land and its people. Therefore, generations of descendants have searched far and wide for every possible cure, compiling them in this book, hoping that one day we can break the family curse and spare future generations from this suffering. Causes There are three hypotheses about the causes of the curse, but none of them have been proven. (I) The Sacrifice Theory. To save the world, the ancestor Graphia had no choice but to trade her own life and the lives of her descendants through the Phantasmoon Games in exchange for the power to duomensionalize a planet in an instant. (II) The Corrosion Theory: During Graphia's battles against the Antimatter Legion, she was struck by enemy forces. The corrosion of Destruction took root deep within her bloodline, cursing the Graphia clan to eternal unrest. (III) The Genetic Theory. The genes of the Graphia ancestors may contain certain hereditary material that causes descendants to have an increasingly higher probability of developing the condition after reaching a certain age phase, ultimately leading to death from the "Weathering Curse." Healing Method There is no cure! To this day, the people of our family have tried many ways, but none of them succeeded. We can only record our failures, to guide future generations in the right direction. Conservative treatment Failed Replacing the weathered body and organs Failed ... Using imagenesis to fill the weathered fissures Failed A line of unreadable text Winning the Phantasmoon Games, borrowing Aha's authority Failed Using The Laughter's Blessing Failed The Technology of the Mourning Actors Failed Xianzhou medical treatments Failed ... Interastral Peace Corporation's genetic treatment Failed The Elixir Seekers' help Failed Find the source of the curse To be confirmed
